name: Vetkoek and mince
summary: Vetkoek (golden fried dough breads), split while hot and filled with gently curried beef mince: a South African favourite for lunch or supper.
about: Vetkoek, Afrikaans for "fat cake", are puffs of yeast dough fried until golden, known as amagwinya in isiZulu and isiXhosa. They are sold from street-corner pots across the country and made at home for weekends and rainy days, split and filled with curried mince, or eaten with jam or syrup.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the lukewarm water and mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough, adding a spoonful more water if it is dry.
Knead on a lightly floured surface for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and springy. Return to the bowl, cover with a damp cloth and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.

Meanwhile make the mince: heat the 2 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the onion for 6–8 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the garlic, curry powder and turmeric and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Turn the heat up to high, add the mince and fry for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned all over.

Add the tomato, carrot, stock and chutney, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring now and then. Stir in the peas and cook uncovered for 5 minutes more, until thick and just moist. Season and keep warm.
Knock the risen dough back and divide it into 12 pieces. Roll each into a ball, flatten slightly and leave on a floured tray for 10 minutes to puff up again.
Heat the deep-frying oil in a deep pot over medium heat to 170 °C, or until a small piece of dough sizzles and rises in about 5 seconds. Never leave hot oil unattended.

Fry 3 or 4 vetkoek at a time for 3–4 minutes a side, turning once, until deep golden and they sound hollow when tapped. Drain on paper towel. If they brown before the middle cooks, turn the heat down.
Split each vetkoek open while warm and fill with a generous spoonful of curried mince.
prepNote: Make the mince a day ahead and reheat. Vetkoek are best fried on the day; leftovers freeze well and refresh in a warm oven.
